title: Redwood discovery - model selection for Acme AI
header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Acme CTO), Maya Singh (Acme ML Eng), Tom Alvarez (PM), Renee Park (Security)
Recording: yes
Links shared: 1) redwood-product-deck.pdf (AE), 2) security-briefing-link (SE)
summary: Discovery focused on model selection for hosted vs dedicated vs private. Customer has high multilingual needs, mixed latency/cost requirements, and tool-calling ambitions. Discussed context lengths, open model comparisons, quantization tradeoffs, and security requirements (SOC2, KMS). Agreed next steps: run a short benchmark with 32k and 128k context, share pricing/architecture options, and send security docs.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share hosted vs dedicated pricing spreadsheet (due: 2025-02-17)
Priya Kapoor: Send performance benchmark template and request for sample prompts (due: 2025-02-14)
Renee Park (Acme): Provide expected data residency/KMS requirements and SOC2 auditor contact (due: 2025-02-18)
Maya Singh: Provide 3 representative prompt sets including multilingual examples (due: 2025-02-14)
next_steps: Redwood to run preliminary CPU/GPU cost & latency estimates for 32k and 128k context models
Schedule a 60-minute SE-led POC scoping session next week
Exchange security docs (SOC2 report, encryption/KMS whitepaper)
Share access to Redwood benchmark harness and instructions to upload sample prompts
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, we have Priya on the call who is our SE to dig into perf and model stuff.
[00:18] Alex: Hi Jordan, hey Priya, thanks, Alex here — CTO at Acme. We wanted to focus on model selection and context needs today.
[00:28] Priya: Great, quick agenda: current stack & constraints, model capabilities (open models comparison), context length needs, multilingual and tool-calling, then security and next steps. Sound good?
[00:40] Tom: Yep, sounds perfect.
[00:47] Priya: Maya, can you kick off with your current stack and pain points?
[00:52] Maya: Sure, so at a high level we run most inference in-house but we are exploring managed options. Primary use case is a customer support assistant — long context, multi-doc summarization, and we also do routing and tool calls to our internal ticketing system. Latency target is 300-600ms tail for short queries but can accept higher latency for long summarization jobs. Cost is a concern.
[01:18] Jordan: Helpful. When you say long context, can you quantify — tokens?
[01:22] Maya: Yes — we have transcripts up to 60k tokens, but the active window we need is usually 20k-40k. There are some research cases where we want 100k+ possible.
[01:36] Priya: Ok that's helpful. Our platform supports a range — hosted models we offer typically up to 32k context for verified model variants, we also have options for 65k/128k with dedicated or private deployments depending on model architecture and quantization. There may be some perf tradeoffs.
[01:55] Renee: From security side we need SOC2 compliance, KMS-managed keys, and VPC access for any private deployment. For hosted we need to understand data retention and encryption in transit & at rest.
[02:08] Jordan: Absolutely — we have SOC2, and we can offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) via KMS for Private deployments; hosted has encrypted tenant isolation and can be configured with strict retention policies. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:22] Alex: On models — we looked at OpenAI g-XXX offerings and Anthropic. We're curious about open model alternatives, particularly Llama-family variants and other 4k/32k/65k open models. Thoughts?
[02:36] Priya: Good question. For open models we often compare Llama 2 variants, Mistral, and newer open weights. Key axes: instruction tuning quality, context window support, inference cost (quantization friendliness), and tool-calling support (function/structured output). Some open models do well on multi-lingual by default, others need instruction tuning or additional tokenizers.
[02:58] Maya: Important for us: Spanish, Portuguese, French, Japanese — we need good coverage.
[03:05] Priya: Llama 2-based variants can be decent, but for out-of-the-box multilingual Mistral and some of the newer open models are stronger. We should benchmark with your actual prompts. Also for 100k+ windows there's limited open options that are efficient; often that requires model families designed with long context or efficient context handling + dedicated infra.
[03:28] Tom: How about tool-calling? We need function calling to call our ticketing APIs and to embed structured actions.
[03:36] Priya: We support function/tool calling patterns in the Redwood API. For hosted models we map to provider function call semantics; for Dedicated/Private you can run models that do local tool calling with lower latency. If you need strict network controls for tool invocations, Private with VPC is safest.
[03:52] Alex: Latency vs cost: what are typical numbers for 32k vs 128k on Dedicated?
[03:59] Samir: Rough ranges — for a 32k-attended forward step on a modern A100/RTX cluster with quantization we really care about batch size and kv cache; p99 latency for a short prompt (under 512 tokens) is usually sub-200ms in Dedicated configs optimized for latency. For 128k context, if you're scanning large windows we see higher memory overhead and increased per-token cost — p99 can be 500ms+ depending on shape. We'll run targeted tests.
[04:28] Alex: Ok. What about accuracy/regression risk when using quantized weights? We've heard hallucination increases with aggressive quant.
[04:35] Priya: Right — aggressive quant (4-bit) can affect instruction-following and subtle generation quality. Our Optimize toolkit helps pick quant profiles per workload; sometimes mixed precision or per-layer quant is best. We'll propose a profile for your summarization workload.
[04:50] Renee: For Private deployment, are audit logs and SSO supported?
[04:54] Jordan: Yes — audit logs, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and integrations with your SIEM are available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted offers SSO and logs, but for full audit isolation Private is recommended.
[05:08] Maya: If we go hosted initially, can we later move to Dedicated without major changes in the app?
[05:14] Priya: Yes — that's one of our differentiators: same API and rollout policies. You can pin model versions and move routes between hosted and dedicated model variants. There are some infra tuning steps but code-level changes are minimal.
[05:25] Tom: You mentioned model variants — do you host both quantized and float variants?
[05:29] Priya: We maintain multiple variants per model. For example a 16-bit float for quality, an 8-bit/4-bit for cost-sensitive workloads, and long-context variants where available. Selection can be route-level so different endpoints pick different variants.
[05:42] Alex: For multilingual benchmarks, how should we send data? Any PI concerns?
[05:47] Jordan: Send anonymized samples through our secure upload link; Priya will send the template. For POC we can sign an NDA if needed and we treat samples per the retention policy we agree.
[06:00] Renee: We'd like to validate KMS flow — BYOK. Can you show that in POC?
[06:06] Priya: Yes, we can include a KMS flow demo in the POC scoping. We typically do a short architecture doc + a lab where we validate key rotation and encryption in transit.
[06:16] Maya: A few technical deep-dive questions — do you support local caching of KV cache across requests for long dialog chains? We want to avoid recomputing encodings for static context.
[06:27] Samir: We have prefix and KV caching mechanisms; for Dedicated/Private you can control cache persistence and TTLs. Hosted supports prefix caching too but with more conservative TTLs. That can significantly reduce token costs for repeated docs.
[06:41] Alex: Regarding tool-calling latency, if the model triggers an external API call, does Redwood block the model or is that asynchronous? We need to orchestrate actions reliably.
[06:51] Priya: The Redwood runtime supports sync and async patterns; for synchronous function calling we can block and return structured payloads. For heavier orchestration we recommend asynchronous flows where the model emits an action and a separate worker executes it, which improves tail latency. We'll design patterns with you.
[07:05] Tom: Any limits on concurrency for Dedicated? We might need a sustained throughput during peak.
[07:10] Samir: Dedicated is configurable — we size GPU pools to meet throughput targets and we offer reserved capacity + burst policies. We'll gather your QPS targets in the POC scoping.
[07:20] Maya: For the open model comparisons, what's the best baseline? Which metrics should we look at?
[07:25] Priya: Baseline: instruction-following (ROUGE/BLEU for summarization is useful but human eval is best), latency (p50/p95/p99), token cost per response, multilingual accuracy on your examples, and hallucination/regression checks on a prompt set. We'll instrument evals and provide dashboards.
[07:47] Alex: Do you have examples of customers who moved from hosted to Private for compliance?
[07:52] Jordan: Yes, we have a couple of enterprise customers in FinTech who started hosted and moved to Private for SOC2 and data residency. Happy to intro references after NDA.
[08:03] Renee: On data residency, do you support EU-only hosting and can you guarantee customer-managed keys in that region?
[08:10] Priya: Yes — for Private deployments we can run the control plane in EU region and configure BYOK with regional KMS. For Hosted we have region options and contractual commitments for data residency. We'll include details in the security docs.
[08:23] Maya: For POC scope, we want to test: 1) 32k summarization flow 2) 65k-ish doc retrieval + summarization 3) multilingual Spanish/French support 4) tool-calling to ticketing API. Is that doable?
[08:37] Priya: Yes, that's a good scope for a 3-week POC. We'll propose a plan: week 0 kick-off & infra, week 1 bench and function calls, week 2 larger-context and tuning.
[08:50] Jordan: Budget/timeline question — are you evaluating for Q2 launch?
[08:54] Alex: We're aiming for pilot in Q2 with a small user group and then ramp in Q3. Cost target is below X per 1k interactions but we can share specifics offline.
[09:05] Samir: We'll model cost per 1k tokens for 32k and 128k contexts and show savings via caching/batching and quantization.
[09:15] Maya: A couple more nitty things — do you support function calling with typed schemas and nested objects?
[09:22] Priya: Yes, function calling supports typed JSON schemas; for deeply nested or streaming tool outputs we have structured output helpers. Sometimes serialization quirks happen with tokenizers — we'll test with your payload.
[09:36] Tom: Are streaming responses supported for long summaries?
[09:39] Priya: Yes, streaming is supported both hosted and dedicated; streaming reduces perceived latency and is useful for long outputs.
[09:47] Alex: Any recommendations on model family for our use case — balancing multilingual, long context, and structured function calling?
[09:54] Priya: Based on what you said, we'd recommend a shortlist: 1) a 32k-optimized instruction-tuned Llama variant for cost-sensitive interactive flows, 2) a Mistral-derived or more recent open weight with strong multilingual performance for non-latency-critical summarization, and 3) a long-context specialized variant (65k-128k) for heavy document retrieval and synthesis — this last one likely runs best on Dedicated/Private. We'll propose exact model names after benchmarking.
[10:20] Renee: On SSO and RBAC, do roles map to team/org constructs? We need separation between Prod and Dev teams.
[10:27] Jordan: Yes, RBAC supports roles and route-level access controls. We'll show example policies in the security pack.
[10:33] Maya: How disruptive is a model rollback if we detect quality regression after a rollout?
[10:38] Priya: We support quick rollbacks via route versioning and can do canary deploys. Our Console also ties regressions to prompt sets so you can detect and roll back fast.
[10:50] Tom: Any gotchas when porting from a hosted model endpoint to on-prem?
[10:53] Samir: Mostly infra: GPU topologies, network, and model IO. We provide an on-prem bundle and orchestration tools. The API layer remains consistent so app code is light.
[11:05] Alex: Great. Let's talk about the benchmark inputs. We'll provide representative prompts — conversational plus the long doc examples.
[11:12] Priya: Perfect — Maya, please use the template. We'll also ask for target latency, p95 target, and expected throughput.
[11:20] Renee: Can you include in the security docs your vulnerability management cadence and logging retention?
[11:25] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll include patching cadences, CVE handling, and retention options.
[11:32] Maya: One more question — do you support vector embedding pipelines co-located with inference to avoid cross-region calls for retrieval?
[11:39] Priya: We can co-locate embeddings + retrieval in Dedicated/Private to minimize cross-region latency. Hosted can also be region pinned, but co-location on Dedicated gives more control.
[11:52] Alex: Anything else from the Redwood side?
[11:55] Jordan: We'll follow up with pricing, security packet, benchmark template, and a proposed 3-week POC plan.
[12:02] Tom: Sounds good. We'll get sample prompts and security requirements to you by Friday.
[12:06] Alex: Thanks everyone.
[12:10] Jordan: Thanks — we'll send notes and next steps.
[12:15] [call ends]
notes: Customer needs: 20k-40k working windows, occasional 100k+ experiments
Multilingual: Spanish, Portuguese, French, Japanese prioritized
Tool calling for ticketing API, require typed schemas and sync/async patterns
Security: SOC2, BYOK, VPC/private deployment option requested
